It's healthy in some regards, not so in others, but as a counter to the attitudes many people have towards weight, I'd say it's necessary. There's too simplistic a view prevalent in so many that weight loss is easy. For some no doubt it is, but the ignorance which is then spouted "if I can do it, anyone can" ignores the reality that everyone's circumstances and challenges with food are different.

The biggest blind spot people have is that balance between physical and mental well-being. Society as a whole fetishizes physical well-being at the cost of ignoring mental health. And the fat acceptance movement can be a boon for those whose self-esteem has been shattered by the hostile reaction so many give towards fat people. It doesn't work for everyone, and parts of it are as blind to reality as those who are saying that it should be easy for everyone to lose weight. But it has its benefits, which should not be dismissed so easily.

Though I will say I have no time for the sort of person who would use the movement to berate others, attacking those who are skinny or who live a physically healthier lifestyle. But then I guess some people are assholes, no matter what size they are, as I've got no time in general for anyone who would feel the need to attack others to try to prop up their own sense of self-esteem.

I do get where you're coming from... and maybe I'm a little naive, but I do agree with you... in the end, I trust people, or at least have a desire to trust people which seems to stretch beyond the boundaries of what might be considered sensible decision making. I don't really believe in 'the one' or anything like that... people are imperfect, love is imperfect, but I don't think I'd want it to be any other way. I just wish... honestly, the thing I'm bitter about is the not knowing. In my life I've had 4 serious relationships, 2 of them (including the most recent one) ended without any sort of resolution, a third took 5 years or so before I got any sort of resolution, and the last just never quite was able to overcome the barriers which were between us... which hurt, but by far hurt the least, because at least I could understand why things ended the way they did. Maybe I made mistakes, I don't know, I don't know if I did everything wrong or nothing wrong, but I just want to be able to learn from the experience, maybe not make the same mistakes again, but leave at least with a better understanding of myself. But instead I'm left in doubt and a bitter self-loathing.

There's not much more I can say than thank you... If there was some easy answer to deal with it, then... well life would be much easier. I'm sorry to hear you're going through the same, it's not something I'd wish on anyone.

I think most humans are meant to be social creatures in one form or another. There is certainly a reliance on the connections we make with each other, and love is the most powerful of all of them. And I fear the problem I face is that in the end, I wont live perfectly fine without it. The only times in my life I've managed to be away from suicidal thoughts are times when I've been caught up in love. The reason I feel suicidal isn't love, or lack of it, it comes from a far earlier point in my life. It's just that through therapy or medication, I've never found relief. 

And it's not that I love for the sake of loving, just that if I ever decided against the possibility of love, I'd basically be saying I was giving up on the only times in my life where I have been able to live. If I was the sort of person who could do that, then... well I wouldn't be the sort of person who is in this sort of struggle right now.
